subject: Recap: ClearingSlate discovery — spend constraints, latency targets, and batching levers
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.inference>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@clearslate.finance>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: ClearingSlate discovery — spend constraints, latency targets, and batching levers

Hi Samir — thanks again for the call today. Wanted to capture a short, action-oriented recap so we’re aligned. Please correct anything I’ve missed.

Key pain points you shared:
- Monthly token spend is unpredictable and recently spiked ~3x on high-concurrency days; finance has capped external AI spend to $50k/mo.
- Latency tail spikes (95th/99th) during peak billing hours are causing poor UX for two workflows: invoice ingestion and customer-facing chat.
- Ops team has limited time to manage model ops — they want low-touch, predictable inference with clear fallbacks.

Goals you’ve prioritized:
1) Stabilize cost so forecasting fits the $50k/mo target (or show a path to replace current vendor while staying within that budget).
2) Reduce 95th/99th latency by 30–50ms for user-facing calls.
3) Run a 6-week pilot that proves unit economics (batching/caching) and produces a sample SLA for production readiness.

Our initial proposal (what we’ll deliver for the pilot):
- 6-week scope: technical spike (2 weeks) + pilot validation (4 weeks).
- TCO spreadsheet with current vs Redwood baseline (we’ll model batching, KV prefix caching, and a quantized 8-bit variant).
- Ops playbook: autoscale policy, fallback path to cheaper variant, and tracing integration.
- Rollout criteria: <50% of current per-token unit cost at expected QPS or clear plan to hit it via batching/route rules.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Samir: share a sample day of token usage and an example latency trace (we referenced a small sample today) — procurement/security asked for it as evidence.
- Procurement: please share your preferred SOW and PO cadence; we’ll draft an SOW for the 6-week pilot and send to procurement + legal.
- Karthik/Marissa: I’ll attach a preliminary TCO workbook and a short pilot SOW draft by EOD tomorrow for your review.

Attachments (initial): ClearingSlate_Token_Econ_v1.xlsx (TCO model), pilot-sow-redwood-draft.docx (SOW stub), latency-trace-sample.txt (anonymized).

Proposed calendar: short technical kickoff next Thursday 10–10:30am PT to validate telemetry access and define the sample dataset. Does that time work?

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.inference | (415) 555-0124

---
From: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@clearslate.finance>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement@clearslate.finance
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: ClearingSlate discovery — spend constraints, latency targets, and batching levers

Thanks Mina — solid recap and exactly what I needed to circulate internally. A few clarifications: 
- The $50k/mo cap is firm for Q3 unless we get a business case; finance is sensitive to any spike risk.
- The ops team can allocate one engineer for ~8 hours/week for the pilot; they can provide telemetry but not deep instrumentation work.
- We definitely want the pilot to include a proof that batching + KV prefix caching can reduce unit token cost by at least 20% without increasing 95th latency beyond our target.

I’ll send a sanitized day of tokens and a short latency sample to you by EOD today (will use procurement alias for the trace). Procurement — if you need any format constraints, let us know.

Yes to the Thurs 10am PT kickoff.

—Samir
Samir Kapoor
Head of Product, ClearingSlate Finance
samir.kapoor@clearslate.finance

On Thu, Jun 17, 2026 at 3:04 PM Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.inference> wrote:
> [original message above]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 12:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: ClearingSlate discovery — internal checklist

Couple internal notes after Samir’s reply: 
- I’ll review the TCO workbook and add a scenario that models: no batching, light batching (2–4 reqs/batch), and heavy batching (8–12 reqs). We should show per-token and per-conversation cost and sensitivity to concurrency.
- Karthik: can you validate whether the proposed 8-bit quantized variant is realistic for their invoice classifier? If not, we’ll swap to fp16 and adjust numbers.
- Ops/eng ask: include a simple fallback policy (route to cheaper variant when queue growth > 20% for 60s) — we can put that in the SOW.

I’ll have a marked-up workbook and SOW comments by tomorrow noon.

—Marissa
Senior FinOps Analyst, Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.inference>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@clearslate.finance>, procurement@clearslate.finance
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Alexa (Sourcing) <alexa@vendorbroker.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: ClearingSlate discovery — next steps and materials (SOW + TCO)

Thanks all — quick update before the kickoff: 
- Attached: pilot-sow-redwood-draft.docx (draft SOW with success criteria), ClearingSlate_Token_Econ_v1.xlsx (initial scenarios), latency-trace-sample.txt (sanitized).
- Action list:
  * Samir/procurement: confirm telemetry delivery method (S3 link vs secure upload) and PO cadence for pilot.
  * Marissa: drop in heavy/light batching lines and sensitivity to concurrency.
  * Karthik: quick feasibility check on quantization path; if you think 8-bit is risky for classifier quality, flag fp16.

If we get telemetry today we’ll instrument a lightweight baseline and share an initial per-token delta by Monday. If procurement is ready we can sign the SOW and start the spike next Wed (23 Jun).

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: pilot-sow-redwood-draft.docx (application/msword), ClearingSlate_Token_Econ_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), latency-trace-sample.txt (text/plain)
